correctness.rationale: The full target-hitting Laplace transform is derived directly, not inferred from a numerical plot: solve the backward modified Helmholtz equation on both sides of the membrane with an absorbing target and the correct flux-continuity/jump conditions. Its explicit denominator agrees with the published Kay-Giuggioli Eq. (11). Independent exponentially timed global resets yield the standard exact iid-trial renewal formula, which produces the stated F(z,B,eta). The representation (exp(z)-1)/z^2=1/z+integral_0^1(1-t)exp(tz)dt and the sum-of-squares expression for the second derivative of (exp(z)+exp(alpha z))/z prove strict convexity for every admissible z,B,eta. Divergence at both ends gives a unique global minimizer. The implicit-function theorem and exact mixed derivative -2eta(1-2B)exp((1-2B)z) prove the universal midpoint maximum; the exact interface derivative and envelope formula prove strict monotonic decline of the optimized mean. The stand-alone standard-library checker independently verifies boundary matching, renewal, derivatives and optimizer trends in 1,461 deterministic assertions; finite checks are corroboration only. No unscreened/restricted protocol ambiguity remains because reset from both sides is explicitly assumed.

originality.rationale: The asserted novelty is the entire global-reset geometry theorem: unique optimal rate, strictly unimodal dependence on the interior membrane location with universal midpoint maximizer, and simultaneous strict decrease of the mean first passage time. The no-reset transform is explicitly credited to Kay-Giuggioli, and the ordinary restart-renewal formula is not claimed. Kay-Giuggioli study membrane first passage without global resetting; both highly relevant Bressloff studies use membrane-screened or side-preserving resetting, not resetting to the exterior from both sides. Their reset clock does not produce independent copies of the full target-hitting experiment and hence does not entail the same derivative law. No equivalent or stronger membrane-position optimum was found in the queried published research record or relevant papers; exhaustive scholarly priority, especially via a generalized restart theorem, remains a risk.
residual_risks: The universal midpoint location may be recoverable as a corollary of a broader general theorem for the sensitivity of optimal stochastic restart; the checked literature did not expose such a dominating statement.

The 2025 moving-barrier article by Telles Timóteo da Silva (DOI 10.1016/j.cnsns.2025.108732) was identified but full text was not available for a direct comparison; its stated moving-barrier setting differs from a fixed semipermeable membrane.
Search coverage is finite, so this is self-review scholarly originality assessment, not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: A structural all-parameter optimization theorem for a natural external-restart physical protocol: barrier position improves the mean monotonically but causes a strict, unique nonmonotone dependence in the optimum reset rate, with the peak forced to exactly half the target-reset distance independently of the permeability. The distinction is experimentally meaningful in externally repositioned diffusion searches with permeable compartments, and distinguishes globally imposed relocation from membrane-screened restart models. There is mathematical substance in deriving the interface transform, proving strict convexity and applying mixed/envelope derivatives uniformly; neither a numerical extremum nor mere recomputation of a known formula is the contribution. No arbitrary parameter slice, value-free constant, or unsupported downstream theorem is claimed.
